subject: Economics
description: Covers RBI functions, Repo Rate, and CRR.

questions.stem: What is the primary objective of 'Monetary Policy' implemented by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)?

options.option_text: To control inflation and regulate the money supply in the economy
To determine the tax slabs for the annual budget
To regulate foreign direct investment (FDI) limits in various sectors
To manage the collection of Goods and Services Tax (GST)

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Monetary Policy is the macroeconomic policy laid down by the central bank (RBI). It primarily involves managing the money supply and interest rates to achieve macroeconomic goals—chiefly keeping inflation in check (around 4% +/- 2%) while also supporting economic growth.
DECOY BUSTING: Determining tax slabs and managing GST are the core functions of the government's FISCAL Policy (handled by the Finance Ministry). Regulating FDI limits is done by the government (DPIIT).
EXAM INSIGHT: The RBI uses tools like the Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, CRR, and SLR to expand (dovish policy) or contract (hawkish policy) the money supply.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: If the RBI wants to curb high inflation in the economy, what action is it most likely to take regarding the Repo Rate?

options.option_text: It will increase the Repo Rate
It will decrease the Repo Rate
It will abolish the Repo Rate entirely
It will keep the Repo Rate strictly at zero

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Repo Rate is the interest rate at which the RBI lends short-term money to commercial banks. To curb inflation, the RBI will INCREASE the Repo Rate. This makes borrowing money from the RBI more expensive for banks. In turn, banks will increase interest rates on loans for the public (home loans, car loans). This discourages borrowing and spending, reducing the money supply and cooling down inflation.
DECOY BUSTING: Decreasing the Repo Rate (making money cheaper) encourages borrowing and spending, which fuels economic growth but can INCREASE inflation.
EXAM INSIGHT: This sequence is heavily tested: High Inflation -> RBI Increases Repo Rate -> Money becomes dearer -> Demand falls -> Prices stabilize.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: What does 'CRR' stand for in the context of Indian banking and monetary policy?

options.option_text: Cash Reserve Ratio
Credit Rating Rate
Currency Regulation Ratio
Central Reserve Repo

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: CRR stands for Cash Reserve Ratio. It is the mandatory minimum percentage of a bank's total deposits that it must keep in cash with the Reserve Bank of India. The bank cannot lend this money out or earn interest on it. It acts as a safety cushion for bank runs and a tool for the RBI to control liquidity.
DECOY BUSTING: 'Credit Rating Rate' and 'Currency Regulation Ratio' are made-up terms. 
EXAM INSIGHT: If the RBI increases the CRR, banks have less money available to lend to the public, which sucks liquidity out of the market and helps control inflation. If the RBI decreases the CRR, it injects liquidity into the market.
questions.subject: Economics

questions.stem: The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), constituted under the RBI Act, 1934, consists of how many members in total, and how are the external members chosen?

options.option_text: Four members, all selected by the RBI Governor and Deputy Governors
Six members — three from RBI and three nominated by the Central Government
Five members — three from RBI and two from the Finance Ministry directly
Eight members — four from RBI and four independent academic economists

questions.explanation: B is correct: the MPC has 6 members — the RBI Governor (Chairperson), one Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, one RBI officer nominated by the Central Board, and 3 external members nominated by the Central Government. Option A is wrong because external members are not chosen by the Governor; Option C is wrong because the Finance Ministry does not directly seat members on the MPC.

questions.stem: Which of the following transactions is specifically classified as an Open Market Operation (OMO) conducted by the Reserve Bank of India?

options.option_text: Revising the Cash Reserve Ratio for all scheduled commercial banks
Purchasing or selling government securities in the secondary open market
Changing the Statutory Liquidity Ratio applicable to commercial banks
Announcing a revision to the key policy repo rate through an MPC meeting

questions.explanation: B is correct: OMOs involve RBI directly buying (injecting liquidity) or selling (absorbing liquidity) government securities in the open secondary market. CRR and SLR changes are quantitative reserve-ratio instruments, not OMOs. Repo rate revision is a price-based instrument decided by the MPC — not an OMO.

questions.stem: The Marginal Standing Facility (MSF), introduced by the RBI in 2011 to provide emergency overnight funds to banks, carries a rate that is typically maintained at:

options.option_text: Equal to the repo rate, with no additional spread or premium charged
Set 25 basis points below the current repo rate as a concessional buffer
Set 25 basis points above the prevailing repo rate, forming the corridor ceiling
Linked to the 91-day Treasury Bill yield and independent of the repo rate

questions.explanation: C is correct: In RBI's LAF corridor, MSF = Repo Rate + 25 bps (ceiling) and SDF = Repo Rate − 25 bps (floor), creating a symmetric 50-bps corridor around the policy rate. Option B describes the SDF rate, not MSF — a common mix-up. MSF is a penal rate for banks that have exhausted other borrowing avenues, so it is set above, not below or equal to, the repo rate.

questions.stem: Among the tools listed below, which one is categorised as a 'qualitative' (selective) credit control instrument of monetary policy, as opposed to a quantitative instrument?

options.option_text: Cash Reserve Ratio — a mandatory reserve requirement prescribed by RBI
Statutory Liquidity Ratio — liquid asset holding norm for commercial banks
Moral Suasion — RBI persuades banks to adjust credit flow to priority sectors
Open Market Operations — RBI buying or selling government securities in market

questions.explanation: C is correct: Qualitative instruments target the direction or purpose of credit (not its volume) and include Moral Suasion, Selective Credit Control, and Margin Requirements. CRR, SLR, and OMOs are all quantitative tools that affect the overall money supply or cost of funds. Candidates often confuse Moral Suasion with direct regulation; it is non-statutory persuasion, which is what makes it 'qualitative'.

questions.stem: India's Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) framework, given legal backing in 2016 through an amendment to the RBI Act, mandates price stability measured by which specific index?

options.option_text: Wholesale Price Index (WPI), covering primary articles and manufactured goods
Consumer Price Index — Combined (CPI-C), reflecting economy-wide retail prices
GDP deflator, which covers the broadest basket of all goods and services
Producer Price Index (PPI), tracking factory-gate prices at the production stage

questions.explanation: B is correct: The Urjit Patel Committee (2014) recommended and the amended RBI Act (2016) codified CPI-C (headline retail inflation) as the FIT anchor at 4% ±2%. WPI was India's earlier informal target but is a wholesale index and excludes services. GDP deflator is too broad and lagged; PPI has not been formally adopted by India as the FIT benchmark.

questions.stem: In April 2022, the RBI activated the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) to replace the fixed-rate Reverse Repo as the floor of the LAF corridor. What is the defining structural difference between SDF and the Reverse Repo mechanism it replaced?

options.option_text: SDF operates at a rate 50 basis points above the prevailing policy repo rate
SDF requires banks to pledge eligible government securities to park funds with RBI
SDF absorbs surplus liquidity from banks without RBI providing any collateral in return
SDF is accessible only to Primary Dealers and not to scheduled commercial banks

questions.explanation: C is correct: Under the old Reverse Repo window, when banks parked money with RBI they received government securities as collateral. SDF is uncollateralised — banks deposit funds with RBI on a clean basis, receiving no G-secs in return. This freed RBI from needing a large stock of securities to sterilise excess liquidity. Option B describes the old Reverse Repo requirement, not SDF. Option A is wrong; SDF = Repo − 25 bps (the corridor floor, not ceiling).

questions.stem: Under the Market Stabilisation Scheme (MSS), the RBI issues government securities and T-bills to sterilise excess liquidity arising from large foreign capital inflows. The funds mobilised through MSS issuances are credited to:

options.option_text: The Consolidated Fund of India, available for routine government expenditure
A separate MSS Cash Account held with RBI, ring-fenced from government spending
RBI's own balance sheet under open market operation sterilisation receipts
The National Investment and Infrastructure Fund for long-term capital deployment

questions.explanation: B is correct: MSS was introduced in 2004 (post-large capital inflows era). Its proceeds are parked in a distinct MSS Cash Account maintained by the Government with RBI and cannot be used for fiscal expenditure — this impounding is what makes sterilisation effective. Option A is the most tempting wrong answer: MSS securities look like regular government securities, leading candidates to assume proceeds flow into the Consolidated Fund, but that would undermine the sterilisation purpose entirely.

questions.stem: The Bank Rate, one of RBI's published policy rates, currently serves as the benchmark for which specific purpose in Indian banking?

options.option_text: Overnight lending to banks under the Liquidity Adjustment Facility
Penal charge on banks for shortfall in SLR or CRR maintenance
Setting the floor rate for all retail lending rates across banks
Determining the coupon on newly issued government dated securities

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Bank Rate today functions primarily as the penal rate charged to banks that fail to maintain the required CRR or SLR, and is aligned with the MSF rate (repo + 25 bps). Historically it was used for direct lending, but that role has shifted to the repo rate under LAF (Option A). Option C confuses it with the External Benchmark Lending Rate framework.

questions.stem: The Urjit Patel Committee (2014), constituted by RBI, recommended a formal inflation-targeting regime for India. Which price index did it recommend as the nominal anchor for monetary policy?

options.option_text: Wholesale Price Index (WPI) — the historically dominant anchor measure
Consumer Price Index — Combined (CPI-C) as the primary nominal anchor
GDP Deflator as a comprehensive economy-wide price level benchmark
Core CPI excluding food and fuel as the most stable price measure

questions.explanation: B is correct: the Urjit Patel Committee recommended CPI-Combined as India's nominal anchor, replacing the ad hoc use of WPI. WPI (Option A) measures producer-side prices and is ill-suited as a welfare indicator. Core CPI (Option D) was considered but rejected because food carries a high weight (~46%) in Indian household budgets and cannot be excluded from the target.

questions.stem: Under RBI's Liquidity Adjustment Facility, Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auctions are conducted to absorb surplus liquidity. How is the cut-off rate in a VRRR auction determined?

options.option_text: Fixed by the MPC at each bi-monthly Monetary Policy Committee meeting
Automatically set at repo rate minus a fixed spread of 25 basis points
Determined through competitive bidding by banks at the market-clearing rate
Linked to the overnight Mumbai Interbank Offered Rate (MIBOR) updated daily

questions.explanation: C is correct: in VRRR auctions, banks competitively bid the rate at which they park surplus funds with RBI; the cut-off emerges at the market-clearing level within a notified range. This contrasts with the earlier Fixed Rate Reverse Repo, where RBI set the rate administratively (similar to Option B). VRRR gives RBI flexibility to absorb durable surplus liquidity at market-discovered rates.

questions.stem: If the MPC fails to keep CPI inflation within the mandated tolerance band of 4% ± 2% for three consecutive quarters, what consequence is prescribed under the amended RBI Act, 1934?

options.option_text: The MPC is dissolved by Central Government and freshly reconstituted
The RBI Governor automatically loses voting rights and MPC chairpersonship
The MPC must submit a report to Government stating causes and remedial steps
The repo rate is mandatorily hiked by 50 basis points per quarter of breach

questions.explanation: C is correct: Section 45ZN of the RBI Act, 1934 (inserted by the 2016 amendment) requires the MPC to submit a report to the Central Government explaining the reasons for the failure, remedial actions proposed, and the estimated timeframe for returning to target. The Act enforces accountability through transparency — not automatic dissolution (A) or mandatory mechanical rate hikes (D).

questions.stem: Under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, commercial banks must maintain the Statutory Liquidity Ratio in eligible liquid assets. Which of the following is NOT a permissible SLR-eligible asset?

options.option_text: Unencumbered central or state government approved securities held freely
Gold held and valued by the bank at prevailing current market price
Cash balances held in accounts with other scheduled commercial banks
Cash maintained in the bank's own vault (till money) as liquid reserve

questions.explanation: C is correct: SLR-eligible assets are (i) cash in hand/vault, (ii) gold at market price, and (iii) unencumbered approved government securities. Balances held with other scheduled commercial banks are NOT SLR-eligible — a common trap since interbank deposits appear liquid but are excluded by statute. Only balances with RBI and own-vault cash count under the cash component of SLR.

questions.stem: When RBI cuts the repo rate, one transmission channel works through the effect on equity and real-estate valuations, which alters household net worth and consumption spending. Which channel does this describe?

options.option_text: Credit channel — banks pass on rate cuts via cheaper loans to borrowers
Asset price channel — lower rates raise equity or property values, boosting spending
Exchange rate channel — rate cuts depreciate rupee and boost export demand
Expectations channel — forward guidance anchors future inflation expectations firmly

questions.explanation: B is correct: the asset price channel works because lower rates raise the present value of future cash flows, inflating equity and real estate prices; higher net worth induces greater consumption (Tobin's q and wealth effect). Option A describes the bank lending/credit channel. Option C is the exchange rate channel working through net exports. Option D is the expectations channel — all four are standard monetary transmission channels and distinguishing them by precise mechanism is a classic examiner test.

questions.stem: RBI's 'interest rate corridor' defines the band within which the overnight call money rate is expected to operate. If the policy repo rate is 6.50%, the SDF rate 6.25%, and the MSF rate 6.75%, which statement about the corridor architecture is precisely correct?

options.option_text: The corridor is asymmetric — 50 bps floor and 25 bps ceiling around repo
The corridor is symmetric — 25 bps on each side of the policy repo rate
The corridor is asymmetric — 25 bps floor and 50 bps ceiling around repo
The corridor spans 100 bps total with repo positioned at its lower bound

questions.explanation: B is correct: with SDF at repo minus 25 bps (floor) and MSF at repo plus 25 bps (ceiling), the corridor is symmetric at ±25 bps around the repo rate — a total corridor width of 50 bps. This design was established when RBI introduced the SDF in April 2022, replacing the fixed-rate reverse repo as the floor. Options A and C describe asymmetric designs that do not match the current framework. Option D incorrectly positions repo at the lower bound rather than the midpoint.
